steps.intent: Our objective is a balanced, humanitarian-focused text that condemns Hamas’s attacks, acknowledges Israel’s self-defence under international law, and demands humanitarian pauses, access, hostage release, protection of civilians and a two-State horizon. The hardest issues will be whether to demand a ceasefire and how explicitly to name Hamas and Israel’s right to self-defence; we have included qualified language on both to secure US/UK support while retaining Arab and Global South backing.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the balanced basis of this draft and welcomes its clear condemnation of Hamas and recognition of Israel's right to self-defence. We ask the penholder to make the hostage paragraph explicit to Hamas and other armed groups and to add an operative condemnation of the use of civilians as human shields. A minor addition on attacks from Lebanese territory would also strengthen the Council's message against regional escalation. With these changes, Albania is ready to vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the Brazilian draft as a basis and welcomes its focus on humanitarian access and protection of civilians. To respond to the gravity of the situation, we ask that OP3 call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, not only pauses, and that the text explicitly demand the lifting of the blockade and rescission of the evacuation order. We also prefer neutral Article 51 language in PP3 to maintain the Council’s impartiality.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the balanced text and welcomes the clear condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and the reaffirmation of IHL and Israel’s right to self-defence within that framework. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 by linking humanitarian pauses to a cessation of hostilities, given the catastrophic situation in Gaza. We would also support a minor addition in OP7 making explicit that de-escalation applies to East Jerusalem as well as the West Bank and the Blue Line.
messages.France: France supports the Brazilian draft as a balanced and credible basis for Council action. It condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence in conformity with international humanitarian law, and addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, including the need for humanitarian pauses and access. We call on all members to unite behind this text without delay.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the humanitarian thrust of the Brazilian draft and thanks the penholder. We ask that OP3 be strengthened from humanitarian pauses to an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire, consistent with our vote on 16 October. We also seek an explicit call for lifting restrictions on humanitarian access and ending the blockade of Gaza so that aid can reach civilians throughout the Strip. Gabon remains ready to work constructively with all Council members.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the current draft as a balanced and comprehensive response to the crisis. It reflects Ghana's priorities: condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks, protection of all civilians under international humanitarian law, urgent humanitarian access, rejection of forced displacement, accountability, and a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. Ghana therefore does not propose amendments at this stage and urges the Council to act with unity and speed.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence consistent with international humanitarian law, and addresses the humanitarian emergency, hostages, and the two-State solution. We ask the penholder to preserve this balance and urge all members to unite behind it.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the current draft as a balanced and action-oriented basis for the Council. It reflects the key elements Malta has consistently called for: condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence within international humanitarian law, the immediate release of hostages, humanitarian pauses and access, rejection of forced displacement, accountability and the two-State solution. We encourage the penholder to preserve this balance and urge the Council to act without further delay.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the humanitarian thrust of the Brazilian draft and would vote in favour, but we believe it must do more to address the catastrophic situation on the ground. We ask the penholder to strengthen OP3 by calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, to demand the lifting of the blockade in OP4, and to call for rescission of the northern Gaza evacuation order in OP5. We also suggest removing the vague military-benefit condition in OP6 so that fuel and essential supplies can reach civilians without undue obstruction.
messages.Russian Federation: The humanitarian thrust of the draft is welcome, but it does not meet the central demand before the Council: an immediate ceasefire. We cannot support a text that substitutes vague pauses for a ceasefire or fails to clearly condemn indiscriminate attacks on Gaza’s civilians and civilian infrastructure. We ask the penholder to incorporate these amendments, including lifting the blockade and protecting civilians, so that the Council can speak with one voice.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the balanced draft and welcomes its condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence within international humanitarian law, demand for the release of all hostages, and call for humanitarian pauses. We ask the penholder to make two targeted additions: explicit ICRC access to hostages in OP2 and accountability for alleged violations by all parties in OP9. With these changes, Switzerland can support the text.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE supports the draft’s condemnation of Hamas attacks, call for hostage release, humanitarian access and rejection of forced displacement. We ask that OP3 reflect the urgency of an immediate and sustained humanitarian pause leading to a cessation of hostilities, and that OP5 explicitly address the evacuation order in northern Gaza as a forcible displacement that must be rescinded. We also seek stronger language in OP6 on lifting restrictions on fuel and humanitarian supplies, including for hospitals and water services.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports the thrust of Brazil's draft and welcomes its clear condemnation of Hamas and recognition of Israel's right to self-defence. We ask the penholder to add explicit condemnation of Hamas's use of civilians as human shields and indiscriminate rocket attacks, and to name Hamas and other armed groups in the hostage-release demand. We can support the text with those changes.
messages.United States of America: The United States appreciates Brazil's efforts and the balanced nature of this draft. We can support the text provided that it explicitly affirms Israel's right to self-defence against terrorism and does not call for a ceasefire. We request the following changes to strengthen the resolution and avoid prejudging sensitive issues like the Al-Ahli hospital explosion.

steps.summary: The revision accepts the United States' red lines on self-defence against terrorism and temporary humanitarian pauses, while incorporating enough humanitarian and accountability language to retain broad support. China and Russia are likely to abstain because the text does not demand a ceasefire, but no permanent member is expected to vote against.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the revised text, which now reflects the core elements we have consistently sought: clear condemnation of Hamas terrorism, recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence, the immediate and unconditional release of hostages, rejection of human shields, and robust humanitarian provisions. We appreciate the penholder’s acceptance of our earlier amendments and urge the Council to speak with one voice. Albania will vote in favour.
messages.China: China appreciates Brazil’s efforts and the partial acceptance of our earlier comments. The current text still falls short on the core humanitarian demand: it provides only for temporary pauses and does not explicitly demand the lifting of the blockade. China requests the changes above and is prepared to support the draft if they are reflected.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the revised text as a balanced and urgent response to the crisis. We welcome the incorporation of work towards a cessation of hostilities and the reference to East Jerusalem, together with the clear condemnation of Hamas attacks and the emphasis on international humanitarian law. We urge all Council members to vote in favour so that the Council can speak with one voice.
messages.France: France supports the draft as it stands. It condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and addresses the humanitarian emergency, protection of civilians, hostages, and the two-State solution. France urges the Council to unite and adopt the text without delay.
messages.Gabon: Gabon welcomes the revised text and the strengthened provisions on humanitarian access. We continue to believe that the Council must call for an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire, not only temporary pauses, in order to silence the guns and prevent further civilian suffering. We also ask that OP5 explicitly call for lifting the blockade of Gaza so that assistance can reach all civilians in need. Gabon is ready to support the text in a vote.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the revised Brazilian draft as a balanced and necessary response to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the need to condemn terrorism and protect civilians. We welcome its emphasis on humanitarian pauses, unhindered access, release of hostages, rejection of forced displacement, and a two-State solution consistent with resolution 2334 (2016). Ghana urges the Council to unite behind this text and will vote in favour if it is put to the vote.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current draft and is prepared to vote in favour. It is balanced: it condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, recognizes Israel’s right to self-defence under international law, demands the release of all hostages, and addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, including through humanitarian pauses and access. Japan urges all Council members to support the text so that the Council can speak with one voice and deliver on the ground.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the revised draft as a balanced basis for Council action. It reflects the necessary condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, recognizes Israel’s right to self-defence within international humanitarian law, and addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation, protection of civilians, hostages, and the two-State solution. Malta therefore encourages all members to support the text and for the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the humanitarian thrust of the revised text and welcomes the inclusion of the rescission of the evacuation order and humanitarian-principles language. However, given the catastrophic situation and our vote on 16 October, we still seek an explicit ceasefire call and a clear demand to lift the blockade. These elements are essential to make humanitarian access meaningful, and we can support the draft with these amendments.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support a text that does not demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire; this remains our red line. We also insist on explicit condemnation of indiscriminate attacks against civilian objects and infrastructure in Gaza and on demanding the lifting of the blockade. Without these changes, we will abstain.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the penholder for accepting our previous requests, in particular the reference to the ICRC in relation to hostage access and the clarification that accountability applies to all parties. The current text reflects Switzerland’s priorities: condemnation of Hamas terrorism, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, immediate release of all hostages, unhindered humanitarian access, respect for international humanitarian law, and a clear rejection of forced displacement. Switzerland supports the draft as it stands and urges the Council to speak with one voice; we will vote in favour if it is put to the vote.
messages.United Arab Emirates: We welcome the incorporation of language on rescinding the evacuation order and on lifting restrictions on fuel and supplies. The text should still move from temporary pauses to durable, sustained humanitarian pauses leading to a cessation of hostilities, and it should demand the immediate rescission of the evacuation order rather than only calling for it. We also seek an explicit call to end the closure regime so that relief can reach civilians sustainably. With these adjustments, UAE can support the draft.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the revised text. It clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law, and calls for humanitarian pauses and unhindered humanitarian access. We thank Brazil for its efforts and urge the Council to unite and adopt the draft.
messages.United States of America: We appreciate Brazil’s efforts to incorporate our key concerns, particularly Israel’s right to self-defence against terrorism and explicit condemnation of Hamas and Hezbollah. To enable us to support the draft, we need OP4 to drop the call to work towards a cessation of hostilities and OP6 to focus on safe passage for civilians who wish to leave rather than rescission of the evacuation order. We also seek a humanitarian-use-only safeguard in OP5 to prevent diversion of assistance.

steps.summary: The revision accommodates the US red lines on OP4, OP6 and OP5 while retaining balanced humanitarian and two-State language. It should secure at least 11 positive votes with no permanent-member negative vote; China, Mozambique, Russia and the UAE are expected to abstain.

reasons.Albania: Albania supported the Brazil draft in the last negotiation round, seeing it as a balanced response that condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks while addressing the humanitarian crisis and Israel’s right to self-defence. As a supportive member, it would likely cast its vote in favour without speaking before the vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil is the penholder and has consistently supported UN Security Council action addressing the humanitarian crisis while recognizing Israel’s security concerns and the need to condemn Hamas attacks. It would vote in favour of its own balanced draft.
reasons.China: China voted in favour to support urgent humanitarian action and a Security Council response, consistent with its record and its calls for a ceasefire and lifting of the Gaza blockade, despite unmet wording requests.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador supported Brazil’s draft in negotiations with no requested changes, and the text reflects Ecuador’s emphasis on condemning Hamas’s attacks, upholding international humanitarian law, addressing the humanitarian crisis, and supporting a two-State solution. A yes vote is consistent with its earlier criticism of the unnegotiated Russian draft.
reasons.France: France supported the Brazilian draft as balanced and consistent with its condemnation of Hamas terrorism, protection of civilians, and humanitarian access priorities. It had no pending amendments or requests and would explain its vote after the vote rather than before.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently supported humanitarian ceasefires and access, including the 16 October draft, and the revised text still advances civilian protection and humanitarian pauses despite not fully meeting its requests. It would therefore vote in favour and, following its practice in the recent comparable vote, would reserve any explanation for after the vote rather than speak before it.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana has supported the Brazil draft and its foreign policy emphasizes humanitarian access, protection of civilians, and the two-State solution. It would vote in favour while condemning violence against civilians by all parties.
reasons.Japan: Japan supported Brazil’s balanced draft, which condemns Hamas terrorism, demands hostage release, calls for humanitarian pauses and access, and reaffirms the two-State solution. As Japan would likely explain its vote after the vote rather than before, it does not take the floor pre-vote.
reasons.Malta: Malta supported the Brazilian draft in the last negotiation round, requested no changes, and the text reflects Malta’s stated priorities on condemnation of terrorism, humanitarian access, protection of civilians and international law.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique’s request was partially accepted and its stated negotiation position was support with changes. As a non-permanent member prioritizing humanitarian protection and Palestinian welfare, it would likely vote in favour while explaining its preference for a stronger ceasefire and blockade-lifting language.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia’s red-line request for an immediate, durable humanitarian ceasefire was rejected, so abstention matches its actual position at the 18 October 2023 vote. It avoids vetoing a text that contains some humanitarian and anti-Hamas language while signalling that the draft remains unacceptable in key respects.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland had already indicated support for the Brazilian draft without requesting changes, and the text reflects its priorities on international humanitarian law, humanitarian access, hostages, accountability, and the two-State solution while condemning Hamas terrorism.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE’s requested changes were only partially accepted, but the draft still advances its priority of urgent humanitarian access, durable pauses, and civilian protection. As an elected member seeking Council unity and relief for Gaza, UAE would vote in favour.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The draft reflects the UK’s public position: condemning Hamas terrorism, affirming Israel’s right to self-defence, and pressing for humanitarian pauses and access. With no outstanding UK requests and prior support in negotiations, the UK would vote in favour.
reasons.United States of America: The draft incorporates the US’s key requested changes, explicitly condemns Hamas, reaffirms Israel’s right to self-defence, and calls only for humanitarian pauses rather than a ceasefire, aligning with US policy and prior negotiating position. Therefore, the United States would vote in favour.

before.Brazil: Brazil has tabled this draft because the Security Council cannot remain passive while civilians, including children, are killed, wounded and deprived of essential supplies. The text is balanced and grounded in international humanitarian law: it condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas, Hezbollah and other armed groups; recognizes Israel’s right to self-defence in conformity with international law; demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; calls for humanitarian pauses and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; rejects forced displacement; and underscores the protection of hospitals, humanitarian personnel and United Nations facilities. It also calls for accountability, including an independent and transparent investigation into the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion, and reaffirms the two-State solution. Brazil will vote in favour and urges all members to support the draft.
before.China:
Mr. President,
China thanks Brazil for its efforts and the consultations on the draft. The situation in Gaza is extremely grave, and a humanitarian catastrophe is unfolding. China condemns all acts of violence against civilians and all violations of international law. The Security Council must take urgent action. The priority is to stop the fighting, end the humanitarian crisis, protect civilians, and ensure rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. China has called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and the lifting of the blockade of Gaza. We also believe that the right of self-defence must not become a justification for excessive use of force. Although the draft before us is not perfect, it reflects the widespread call of the international community and the Council’s responsibility. China will vote in favour. We urge all parties to implement its provisions and to work for a just and lasting solution based on the two-State solution and relevant United Nations resolutions.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador thanks Brazil for its efforts to conduct inclusive consultations and to present a balanced text. We will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires the Security Council to speak with one voice. Ecuador condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups against Israel, as well as all acts of violence against civilians. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access; humanitarian pauses respected by all parties; the protection of medical facilities, humanitarian workers and United Nations personnel; and the rejection of any forced displacement of civilians. Ecuador reiterates its commitment to a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We call on all Council members to support this resolution and on all parties to implement it without delay.
before.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour of this draft resolution. We condemn all acts of terrorism and violence against civilians, including the attacks by Hamas on 7 October and indiscriminate rocket fire against Israel. We remain gravely concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the alarming loss of civilian life. Ghana calls for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the unconditional release of all hostages, and the protection of medical facilities, United Nations personnel and humanitarian workers. We reject any forced displacement of civilians and stress the need for accountability and independent investigations, including into the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion. Ghana reaffirms its commitment to a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution and relevant United Nations resolutions. We support this resolution as a step to alleviate suffering and pursue peace.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. The text includes essential elements that Malta has consistently stressed must be addressed: the strongest condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas on Israel; Israel’s right to self-defence in full conformity with international humanitarian law; the protection of all civilians, especially children; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the need for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including the lifting of restrictions on essential supplies; the rejection of forced displacement; and accountability for violations, including the reported explosion at the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital. Malta remains convinced that the Security Council must speak clearly and act to save lives, alleviate suffering and preserve the prospects of a two-State solution. We thank Brazil for its efforts and call on all members to support this text.
before.Mozambique:
Mr. President,

Mozambique remains gravely alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the alarming loss of civilian life, including women and children, the destruction of civilian infrastructure, and the attacks on hospitals, United Nations facilities, schools and humanitarian personnel. My delegation condemns all attacks against civilians and all acts of terrorism, and stresses that all parties must comply fully with international humanitarian law and international human rights law.

We support the draft resolution before the Council as an urgent step to protect civilians, demand the release of hostages, reject forced displacement, and ensure rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza. Mozambique has consistently called for an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire and for the immediate lifting of the blockade of Gaza. While the text does not fully reflect those essential calls, we believe it is imperative that the Council act now, rather than remain silent in the face of a humanitarian catastrophe. We therefore vote in favour of this draft resolution and urge all parties to implement its provisions without delay.

Thank you.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will abstain on this draft. We have consistently insisted that the Security Council must send a clear and unambiguous signal in favour of an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire. Regrettably, the text before us still lacks this central demand. It also does not reflect our proposed amendments to condemn indiscriminate attacks against civilian infrastructure in Gaza, including hospitals, schools and United Nations facilities, and to demand the lifting of the blockade of the Gaza Strip. We do not deny the humanitarian intentions of the penholder, but a resolution that fails to stop the bloodshed and does not address the root causes cannot be supported by our delegation. We call for genuine collective action to end hostilities and to protect civilians.
before.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks Brazil for its efforts to find a balanced text. Switzerland will vote in favour. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups, the taking of hostages, and all indiscriminate attacks against civilians. We are gravely concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the loss of civilian life, including at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital. This Council must demand full respect for international humanitarian law, the protection of civilians and medical and humanitarian personnel, the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and humanitarian pauses. The text also rightly rejects forced displacement, calls for accountability and independent investigations, and reaffirms the two-State solution. Switzerland will continue to support every effort to de-escalate and protect civilians.
before.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We thank Brazil for its efforts to forge a text that responds to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and to the need for Council unity. We welcome the inclusion of durable and sustained humanitarian pauses and the call to ensure the sustained opening of all crossings for humanitarian relief. We regret that other important elements were not retained, including a clear demand for the immediate rescission of the evacuation order and an end to the closure regime of the Gaza Strip. Nevertheless, given the scale of the suffering and the urgent need to protect civilians, secure the release of all hostages and allow life-saving assistance to reach those in need, we support this resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Mr. President, the United Kingdom votes in favour of this resolution. We unequivocally condemn the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups against Israel, and we support Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law. We also stress the urgent need for humanitarian pauses, full and unhindered humanitarian access, the immediate release of all hostages, and the protection of civilians, medical facilities and humanitarian workers. The situation in Gaza is catastrophic, and this Council must speak with one voice. We welcome Brazil’s balanced text and urge all parties to comply with their obligations under international humanitarian law.

after.Albania:
Mr. President,

Albania voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. In the face of the heinous terrorist attacks by Hamas of 7 October and an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza, the Security Council could not remain silent. This text is balanced and reflects the core elements we have consistently insisted upon: the strongest condemnation of Hamas terrorism and indiscriminate attacks against civilians; recognition of Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in full conformity with international humanitarian law; the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; the protection of civilians, hospitals, United Nations facilities and humanitarian personnel; and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including through humanitarian pauses.

Albania has been clear from the outset: terrorism cannot be justified, and it cannot be allowed to set the agenda. But the protection of civilians is equally non-negotiable. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution. We reject any forced displacement of civilians. There must be accountability for all violations, including the reported explosion at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital, through a thorough, independent and transparent investigation.

We regret that the Council could not speak with full unanimity, but the adoption of this resolution is an important step. Its value will now depend on full and immediate implementation. Ultimately, there is no military solution to this conflict. Albania reaffirms its support for a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and recognised borders based on the 1967 lines, in accordance with resolution 2334 (2016). We will continue to engage constructively and actively in the Council to protect civilians, uphold international law and advance that goal.
after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil welcomes the adoption of this resolution. The Security Council has at last responded to the catastrophic situation in Gaza and to the urgent need to protect civilians. We thank all delegations whose engagement strengthened the text, and we welcome the broad support it has received.

Our responsibility does not end with this vote. Brazil calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses; for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, including through the Rafah crossing; and for the protection of civilians, hospitals, medical personnel, humanitarian workers and United Nations facilities. All parties must comply with international humanitarian law. We reject any forced displacement of civilians and call for accountability for all violations, including through an independent and transparent investigation of the explosion at the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital.

Brazil will continue to work with Council members and regional partners to translate this resolution into action, to de-escalate the conflict and to preserve the prospect of a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution and resolution 2334 (2016). Thank you.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China welcomes the adoption of this resolution. We thank Brazil for its efforts to build consensus. At a time when Gaza is facing an unprecedented humanitarian catastrophe, the Security Council must not remain silent. The adoption of this text, though not perfect, sends a clear signal that the international community is united in demanding the protection of civilians and an end to the violence.

The most urgent task now is full and effective implementation. China calls on all parties to immediately cease hostilities, exercise maximum restraint, and spare no effort to protect civilians, especially children, women, medical personnel, United Nations personnel and humanitarian workers. Israel must comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and the right of self-defence cannot justify excessive use of force or collective punishment of the Palestinian people. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and call for full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need in Gaza. The blockade must be lifted, border crossings opened, and restrictions on essential supplies, including fuel, food, water and medicine, removed.

China is gravely concerned by attacks on hospitals, schools and United Nations facilities, including the explosion at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital. A thorough, independent and transparent investigation is necessary, and all violations of international law must be held to account. We reject any forced displacement of Palestinian civilians.

The Palestinian question is at the heart of the Middle East issue. The current crisis once again shows that the status quo is unsustainable. China will continue to support the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders based on the 1967 lines, and will continue to support the just cause of the Palestinian people in realizing their legitimate national rights. China is ready to work with Council members and the international community to de-escalate the situation and advance a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in the Middle East.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of the resolution submitted by Brazil and welcomes its adoption. At a time when the Security Council must shoulder its responsibilities, this text sends a clear message: the terrorist attacks carried out by Hamas and other armed groups against Israel on 7 October must be condemned in the strongest terms, and Israel has the right to defend itself, in full conformity with international humanitarian law.

The protection of civilians is imperative and must be ensured by all parties. France demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses; and full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need throughout Gaza, including through the opening of all necessary crossings and the lifting of restrictions on essential supplies for humanitarian use. Hospitals, medical personnel, humanitarian workers, United Nations personnel and facilities must be protected. France rejects any forced displacement of civilians.

France also recalls the need for an independent, transparent and thorough investigation into the explosion at Al-Ahli Arab Hospital and for accountability for all violations of international law. All parties must respect international humanitarian law, including the principles of distinction, proportionality and precaution.

France calls for de-escalation, including along the Blue Line and in the West Bank, and reaffirms its commitment to the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, in accordance with resolution 2334 (2016). The adoption of this resolution must now be translated into action on the ground. France will remain fully engaged to that end.
after.Gabon:
Mr. President,

Gabon voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by Brazil and welcomes its adoption. We did so because the Security Council could not remain silent in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, the alarming loss of civilian life, and the suffering of civilians, especially women and children.

Gabon unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups against Israel, as well as all acts of violence and indiscriminate attacks against civilians. We demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and their humane treatment.

We call on all parties to comply fully with international humanitarian law and to protect civilians, medical personnel, hospitals, United Nations personnel and facilities, schools and humanitarian convoys. The calls in this resolution for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses, full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the opening of crossings, including Rafah, and the lifting of restrictions on essential supplies must be implemented without delay.

Gabon rejects any forced displacement of civilians. We also support an independent, transparent investigation into the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion and accountability for all violations of international law. The Council must remain engaged in the search for a just and lasting peace based on the two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognized borders, in accordance with resolution 2334 (2016). Gabon will continue to support all efforts to silence the guns and alleviate the suffering of civilians.
after.Japan: Japan voted in favour of this resolution and welcomes its adoption. The Security Council has spoken with one voice at a time of grave crisis, and that unity must now be translated into action on the ground. Japan condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other armed groups against Israel, including the taking of hostages, and affirms Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law. At the same time, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is catastrophic. All parties must comply with international humanitarian law, protect civilians, and respect medical personnel, hospitals, United Nations personnel and facilities. Japan demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and calls for immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian pauses, as well as full, rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Gaza. We reject any forced displacement of civilians and stress the need for accountability, including through an independent and transparent investigation into the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion. Japan urges all parties to avoid further regional escalation and remains firmly committed to the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and resolution 2334 (2016). Japan will continue its diplomatic and humanitarian efforts to help protect civilians and advance a just and lasting peace.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States voted in favor of this resolution because the Security Council must speak with one voice in the face of Hamas’s terrorist atrocities and the catastrophic humanitarian crisis in Gaza. We thank Brazil for its constructive efforts and for engaging all Council members. This text condemns Hamas’s terrorist attacks, demands the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, recognizes Israel’s right to self-defense in accordance with international law, and calls for humanitarian pauses and rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access for civilians in need.

Let me be clear: there is no equivalence between Hamas terrorists and the State of Israel. Hamas bears responsibility for the suffering it has unleashed. It uses civilians as human shields and embeds military infrastructure in civilian areas. That is why Israel has the right to defend itself, and it must do so in full respect for international humanitarian law, including the protection of civilians and medical facilities.

The United States is working intensively to deliver lifesaving assistance, open humanitarian corridors and secure the release of hostages. Humanitarian supplies must reach those in need and must not be diverted by Hamas or any other armed group. We also call for a thorough investigation into the Al-Ahli Arab Hospital explosion and for all parties to avoid further escalation in the region. The Council’s words must now be translated into action. We reaffirm our commitment to the two-State solution and to a future in which Israelis and Palestinians live in peace and security.
